utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Registrar would you have the accused brought in, please (The accused was brought in).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Does everybody hear? Prosecution, defence, does everybody hear? Mr. Blaskic, do you hear me. THE DEFENDANT: Good morning, your Honours, I hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. We can then have the witness brought in, and continue with the cross-examination with Mr. Nobilo. Mr. Djidic (continued)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are you well rested, everything all right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President, your Honours. Good morning, Mr. Djidic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We had stopped with the document on the Croatian Muslim Defence Council, which was your initiative. I should now like to ask you to try to recall another initiative for the formation of some kind of union of armed forces, namely, do you know anything about a joint command Pasalic, Prkacin, two high ranking officers, when this was and anything about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. I think somewhere around the month of October Mr. Pasalic came to Travnik as well as Mr. Jaganjac and Mr. Prkacin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: To make it clearer to the court, can you tell us who these gentlemen were, what their rank was and who they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were senior officers, colonels, and I think they were officers who had come from Croatia. I know that Mr. Prkacin had come from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me, we are not really hearing this very well. Perhaps there is some kind of interference. Somebody seems to be very happy, seems to be whistling. It does disturb the serenity of our hearing when we hear whistling like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So and that Prkacin came from Croatia what armed formation did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was in the HVO or the Croatian army, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, what about Arif Pasalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was in the army, in the TO, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And when did you see these gentlemen for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was in October.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where did you meet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was this a meeting? Can you explain what was happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a meeting, held both in Travnik and in Vitez. The task of these men was to link together the units of the army and the HVO, and to try to defend Jajce.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was there any command by a higher left command of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, for instance, giving them such instructions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall, but I do not think they could have come on their own initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we describe this as a joint command in central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we could. It could be called that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And how did that function? How long did it last, and what was the outcome of this joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It functioned until the date that Jajce fell. I think that for some time after that these gentlemen stayed on, but I do not know what happened afterwards, where they went.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can it be said that in this period the joint command was superior to Blaskic or the command of the Third Corp, for instance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whether they were superior but while they were present there, there were meetings of all the commanders, from central Bosnia, Croats and Muslims, or rather the HVO and the TO. At one of those meetings both in Vitez and in Travnik I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And how would you assess this episode with the joint command of Pasalic Prkacin was that a positive endeavour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Any attempt along those lines at that time was a good one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Therefore your assessment is positive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that Muslim hotels and restaurants in Vitez were blown up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Which hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim cafes, Muslim shops, such as kiosks, stores, and houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And a hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The hotel in Kruscica was attacked, Hotel Plavac, and on that occasion considerable damage was inflicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How was it attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The hotel was rented by a Muslim. It was a hotel that was owned by the work organisation called Sebesic. At the time Sebesic was renting out its facilities for a certain compensation to private people, individuals, or rather to their own employees.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You did not tell us how it was attacked, how the hotel was attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The hotel was attacked with RPG shells, when considerable damage was done. I was not an eyewitness, so I do not know the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When was this in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you list the other cafes and bars owned by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a bar on the bridge across the Lasva river owned by Najlo Hodzic. It was blown up twice. Then several other bars in the city itself, the kiosk, which was in the close vicinity of the hotel. Then a hairdressers owned by Zumreta Kalazovic, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who were the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The perpetrators were never identified. We never received any report to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was any Croatian facility blown up of a similar kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think not. I am not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me try to refresh your memory. The Kamin restaurant, on 29th January 1993. Do you remember that event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who is the owner, a Croat or a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The owner of that facility was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it -- was an explosive planted there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was, and there were various rumours about that event.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was the perpetrator identified?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was not, but there was talk, I think even at the crisis staff, and we received a report that was not confirmed, that the owner of that bar refused to pay some money to the HVO. This is not something that I personally heard, so, as I said, they are just rumours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, this would be a case of the Croats blowing up Croatian facilities and the other was the Croats blowing up Muslim facilities? I should like to show you a document regarding the superior command. So, can the usher help me, please? (Handed). Mr. Djidic, will you place the document under the ELMO so that the others can see it and I will try to read it, and you can look at it. In the heading it says "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Croatian community of Herceg-Bosnia, Croatian Defence Council, command of the 4th battalion of military police, Vitez. Number 02-4/3-07-68/93. Date: January 18th, 1993. Addressed to, on the right-hand side, to the head of the military police master operative zone central Bosnia." And the heading is "report on a killing". Then we come to the text: "On 17th January, 1993 at about 10.30 pm Srecko Veber a driver in the command of the Fourth Battalion of military police in Vitez was killed. The killing of the military policeman took place in the cafe Pizzeria Venezia in Travnik, according to eyewitness reports. The investigation on the spot was carried out about 2 am on the 18th January, 1993, in the Venezia cafe, in Travnik, in the presence of military judge Zeljko Percinlic military prosecutor Marinko Jurcevic. Operative criminal investigator Nikola Opadak and crime investigating technician Marinko Jurcevic. In addition to the above mentioned the investigation of the crime scene was attended by representatives of the MUP Travnik Ferzo Daelilbarsic, Nermin Megimovic, Nikola Augustinovic and a military judge of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina Darmin Avdic. According to eyewitness reports the murder was committed by Enveroa Dlelibasic from Karaula, a member of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina who is a fugitive. An arrest warrant has been issued for Enveroa Dlelibasic. Signed by the commanders Zvouko Vukovic, the stamp of the command of the military police from Mostar, and it says copies to the Signal Centre Vitez, the operative zone of central Bosnia and the archives. Mr. Djidic, do you recall this event now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you recall in connection with this event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that there had been some problems in Travnik; that there had been killing, but I do not know the details about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The person killed belonged to the military police in Vitez. Did it provoke any negative reactions? Did you discuss this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there were some discussions. I do not recall the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know Janko Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I do, but I cannot clearly remember his face.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But you know the post he held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he worked in the military police, in the regional police of the HVO in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And these persons listed here, for instance, members of MUP Travnik, are they familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about the military judge of the BH army Avdic Darmin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know him, even now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And from Vitez the judge and Prosecutor, Zeljko Percinlic and Marinko Jurcevic, do you know them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had heard of them. I do not know whether I know them well, in person, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Defence would like to tender this document under the same conditions as those tendered yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is just under the same conditions, Mr. President, that without any source it is not to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, the Defence has just said that this should be filed under the same conditions as yesterday. Let me remind you of the conditions of yesterday that any document that -- these documents would be provisionally listed as D19 and the Tribunal said that the identification had to be done. I suppose, at some other time. Mr. Nobilo, another time during the trial you will identify the document otherwise it will not be considered by the Tribunal to be an exhibit. We agree on this, do we not? I hope we do not have to repeat the same thing every time otherwise we will waste time. All right then, this will be D what?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. President, the Defence has no other choice but to accept. Mr. Djidic, you said that there were no violence committed by members of the BH army against Croats. You mentioned the example of your acquaintance or friend from the police who returned and was killed, because he believed that the situation would improve. Let me ask you a few questions to refresh your memory regarding the situation as it existed at the time. Do you remember that on the 10th December, 1992, in Kruscica, that is within your municipality members of the BH army shot at a vehicle of the Vitez HVO and wounded a person in doing so? This is the 10th December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But do you know that the event took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was some talk about something, but I think that the perpetrators were not identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 17th January, 1993, in Vitez, in a locality called Sadovace, members of the BH army disarmed a member of the HVO, confiscated their vehicle TAM 110 and two cases of explosives. Do you remember that incident, that took place on 17th January in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were many incidents. This particular one regarding this vehicle is something I do not remember. If I had more details about it, perhaps I could remember better. I apologise. I already told you that in those days, that is somewhere from November onwards, a brigade had been formed, the 325th brigade, and with the formation of that brigade I lost certain competences, so that I was not informed, in detail, about certain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, I understand that, but you were present there, so I am just asking whether you remember. It need not be a question of your competence. Do you remember that on 21st January, 1993 Kruscica municipality of Vitez, members of the BH army fired at Croatian houses and wounded an HVO member? This was January 21st, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is something very close to you. On that same day, the 21st January 1993 in Stari Vitez, members of the BH army stopped two military policeman, maltreated them, and cursed their Ustasha mothers. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On 20th November 1992 in Kruscica Vitez municipality members of the BH army carried out a massacre, it says here, of six members of the military police, confiscating their weapons, insignia and money. Do you remember that event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Will you please repeat the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The 20th November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was this the event that you have already described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was when two members of the army were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You have already explained that, so we will not go into any further details.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On 8th November, 1992 in Vitez near the Fire Brigade building, I think that was where your command was, members of the BH army fired at Jarko Biljaka, an HVO member and injured him seriously. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My command was not there, my headquarters. This was in front of the station of the civilian police. But I am familiar with that event.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you know about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that this young man Biljaka provoked an incident. I am not sure. I think that he even threw a bomb, a grenade. After that he was shot at, and we spoke about this at a meeting. I heard that he was wounded. How badly, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You say you are not sure about the bomb. How could you mistake something like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time there were many awful things happening and Mr. Biljaka had a reputation for that sort of thing in Vitez. I think he caused trouble with the Croats as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So as far as the bomb is concerned, what shall we conclude? Do you remember or do not you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he did throw that bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: With any degree of certainty or with a reservation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With a reservation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Another incident in Vitez. On 26th June, 1992, members of the BH army from Vitez murdered Boznera Vitza and Shunka Narkov and whose bodies were buried and recovered after 45 days. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you know about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that there were -- the intention was to accuse the TO troops. I think that the Territorial Defence troops did not do that. I think it was rather a settlement of old scores between Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So it is again the scheme of Croats against Croats violence. On 10th September, 1992, members of the BH army from Vitez were guilty of robbery and later murder of Plavcic Iva, do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The perpetrators were not TO troops. First of all, we did not know who the perpetrators were. Later that was discovered and that act has been unanimously condemned by everyone in Vitez. At that time there was even co-operation with the Croats. Since I am now working in the Ministry of the Interior, a few days ago I received information of the sentence brought against two members, Bosniaks who were guilty of that murder, who committed that murder. That act had no justification whatsoever at that time, although at that time we did not know who these people were. We had our ideas. The last suspicions have only now been dispersed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: After five years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I received the verdict, I think, 20 days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you remember an event which took place on the same day, the 10th September, 1992, when members of the then Territorial Defence, later the BH army, killed Ivica Stojak commander of the HVO from Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were the killers arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And in your municipality that murder of the HVO commander from Travnik, did it have any effect? Did it have an impact at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my testimony I said that there was constant tension in our area, in those days, and I cannot recall exact the dates and the details; but after such incidents soldiers of the HVO were frequently making trouble, on top of the trouble they had been making before.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, but on several occasions, until now you mentioned that BH army members never did anything against HVO troops or Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that, and I am prepared to reiterate that now. But when I spoke in my testimony I spoke of the Vitez municipality. What we have just discussed were solitary and out of character events, uncontrolled events, which were minor compared to what the Croats were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But there were such incidents, despite your statement of a few days ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The question I was asked was: "was this done by TO members?" And I said: "no". The murder we have mentioned was committed by people in mufti, people who are not on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But 6 Ivica Stojak was killed by members of the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ivica Stojak was not killed on the territory of the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you have a special army in Vitez or was a part of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What we had in Vitez was the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence. As in every other municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Separated from the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina or an integral part of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An integral part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Namely, maybe you did not understand me correctly, but I did not finish with this one. On 12th February, 1993, members of the BH army from Vitez killed Sasa Jurisic. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the moment I cannot call.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Sasa Jurisic from Vitez, 12th February 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The 15th March, 1993, in Vitez, close to the Max shop, members of the BH army threw hand grenade injuring a woman and a child and causing major material damage. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, I will. The 15th March, 1993. Shop named Max, a woman and a child wounded by hand grenade, that is not a -- not an unusual event -- not an usual event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I recall that, but I am not quite sure. If you mean the same thing that I have in mind, that hand grenade was thrown by TO members who also were not on duty at the time, but the hand grenade was thrown at a Muslim, a member of the civilian police. The hand grenade was thrown by the brothers of the policeman's wife. In fact his ex-wife, because they were divorced then. And his ex-wife and child were then wounded. That was a settlement of scores between Bosniaks, that is Muslims as far as I remember, if you have it in your document. If you have these details in your document, I think the bomb was thrown on Mr.s Adnan Adilovic -- I am sorry , on Mr. Adilovic and his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But the only people wounded were a woman and a child?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was the woman a Croat a Bosniak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know for sure. I think it was his wife who was hurt, I am not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Donja Veceriska is in your municipality. Do you remember 16th March, again 1993, members of the BH army threw a hand grenade through the entrance of the HVO command. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you describe that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was done by a young man intoxicated at the time. We had tried to take him into custody several times because he had tried to throw a hand grenade on policemen. I think he disarmed my own police. It was a man with an inclination to such behaviour when under the influence of alcohol. I think on that occasion nobody was hurt, at least no Croats were hurt. His house is across the road from the office of the HVO command in Donja Veceriska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How would you appraise the impact of that incident on the Croat Bosniak relationship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not approve of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But did it aggravate the tension?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The tension existed before that, and the HVO was grateful to us for detaining this man.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: All right. But the day before, again in Donja Veceriska a member of the BH army shot from infantry weapons a member of the HVO in Donja Veceriska, that is the same place, just the day before, and the same day there, the shooting of the command, members of the BH army harassed passers-by and drivers and also committed shooting, injuring several people. That happened the day before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Again in Donja Veceriska, on 24th March, eight days later, members of the BH army shot at private houses owned by Croats. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On 10th April 1993, six days before the beginning of the conflict, in Vitez, in the vicinity of the BH army command, members of the BH army detained Sucic Ivo and Maric Slavko who were in civilian clothing and coming back from the church, members of the HVO, but off duty, they were maltreated and then released, the 10th April 1993, near the command of the HVO -- near the command of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that. Ivo Sucic was a friend of mine. I talked to him personally after that incident. That was not committed by a member of the army. I condemned that incident, and I am still against such behaviour. That particular act was committed by a Muslim who was inebriated. I think he did not even know at the time who he was quarreling with.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You talked about the Vitez barracks. Do you remember 12th April 1993 when in the building of the police when they were headquartered, they threw a bomb and from infantry weapons attacked the building where the Vitovoe were billeted. All vehicles with HVO markings were on that day attacked from infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In April, but that was on the next day, on 12th April, not long before the conflict again in Travnik, commander of the Vitez army barracks, Vitez army headquarters was attacked. He was disarmed and attacked by five military policeman. Do you know anything about that? Did it have an impact in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know about that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does the name Darko Kraljevic ring any bells? Did you hear about that case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I know who the man is but I did not hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the next day, three days before the conflict, again it was Darko Kraljevic, commander of the Vitez army barracks, excommander of HOS, members of the BH army attempted murder of Darko Kraljevic and his escort. They managed to run away with the member of the UNPROFOR, despite the fact that they were -- that they were ambushed. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you know about that event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I received a telephone call from Mario Cerkez that day, and he told me, and he told me that he spoke on the walkie-talkie with Kraljevic and that after that they were disconnected. He assumed that there was trouble of some kind. He asked me to try to do something and see what was going on. I contacted the command of the brigade and told them that we should form a joint patrol with the participation of the police, members of the army and HVO, and that is what we did. The patrol went to inspect the crime scene, so to speak. They found the vehicle Kraljevic was driving and not far from the vehicle Kraljevic, and it seems to me they also found Bagrem Zolat who was Kraljevic's colleague. In any case, a commission visited the spot, found their vehicle, established that the vehicle had been shot at, but they did not know who the shooters had been. I think that is still a mystery, to this day. Kraljevic had said he assumed he had been shot at by army members. After that he intensified arrests of Muslims, both civilians and troops. And at that time there were many Muslims in jail, in the school building in Dubravica, both civilians and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Have you ever been in that school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, before the war, I did -- I was, and my children went there to school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I mean at the time of the event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you do not know -- you did not see that scene?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not, but I have reports from people who were detained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What kind of man was Darko Kraljevic, what would you say about him? What kind of unit did he have? Could you tell us more about him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could speak a lot about Darko Kraljevic. I used to be his teacher. I told him how to ski and he took part in cycling contests. That was before the war, when he was still a teenager. At the time when the HOS was being established he was a rowdy character. He went to the front to fight the Chetniks. But he was surrounded by people with troubled pasts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean people of shady character, people who are using alcohol and drugs, and criminals. I am not saying all of them were like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was the nickname of their unit when they abandoned the name of HOS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they changed their name to Vitozovi, which means Knights.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That unit was it involved in any crime, because if people had a criminal past that still does not mean that once they joined the army and were in a war that they could not have changed. What was their behaviour then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the war, as far as I know from the period when I was still in Vitez, I have been attacked several times by the Vitozovi units and they were part of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When were you attacked by the Vitozovi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 16th April, in early morning hours when the entire territory of the municipality was under attack, the Vitozovi took part in this attack. There were other attacks in the course of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you give us another date when you were attacked, specifically by the Vitozovi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they were in joint units with the HVO, and on the 18th July they participated in the attack against Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you see who led the attack against Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That was an 18th July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Have you noticed the Vitozovi specifically as one leading an attack on another occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that during that war the Vitozovi were sort of melted into the HVO structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you tell us when did that happen? When did they blend with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Immediately before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you mean, in terms of dates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think in the spring of 1993, and also in the autumn of 1992, the Vitozovi would do the dirty work for the HVO authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I asked when they were incorporated into the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think this was during the days of the general attack at the beginning of the war. I may not be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The beginning of the war was 16th April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like to mention another incident, if we can call it that, and ask you what you know about it and what its effects were. Namely, are you aware of the event of 15th April, just before the outbreak of the conflict in Vitez? On 15th April, in Zenica the commander of the HVO of Zenica, Zivko Totic was kidnapped as well as four members of his escort were killed, and another person who happened to be a witness. What do you know about the consequences of that event, and the event itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard about the event, I think on 16th or 17th April, when the attack on Vitez had already begun. I heard about it from HVO officers. I think the man in question was Marko Prskalo, and one of the conditions for the discontinuation of the attack on Vitez was the release of Zivko Totic from detention, but Vitez had absolutely nothing to do with his arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about the army of the H, what did it have to do with this kidnapping?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of it. To this day, I do not know who was behind it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you did not hear that the Mujahedin foreigners from Arab countries had kidnapped Zivko Totic and addressed a letter to the HVO command demanding the release of their own comrades Mujahadin, in return?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not hear of that. I think Prskalo said it was the army who had captured Totic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But the Mujahedin were part of the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a sense, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So it was the army after all?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour, I object to the last comment. I object to Mr. Nobilo's last comment about "So, it is the army after all". That is Mr. Nobilo's conclusion. That was not a question and that was not the witness' answer. I move to strike that comment and I object to his comments of that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, after the witness, having given a different answer several times my question was "So, it was the army after all" and the witness answered "yes", so it was a question. There are many such questions that contain the answer in them, used by the Prosecutor, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think a review of the transcript will indicate that that is not the case. It is on the screen right now "So it was the army after all", as he is about to move into the next conclusion. That was not a question that was Mr. Nobilo's statement. The point of the matter, Mr. President, is I object to Mr. Nobilo's editoralising on the witness' answer. The questions are fine editorialisings the Prosecution objects to. That is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. Mr. Nobilo must limit his comments. I would like to say to you, Mr. Kehoe, that you must also commit yourself not to make any comments. Let me point this out to you. Let me remind you in the examination and cross-examination either of you some time make implicit or explicit comments because each of you have a strategy you are following. Be tolerant to one another and attempt to limit your comments, Mr. Nobilo. Proceed, please. If you are continuing with this same incident you can end now -- you finish your questions otherwise we will take our break now. Have you completed that incident, in inverted commas, that of that date?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, since the witness mentioned the name of Marko Prskalo from whom he received the information I have only one question regarding this person then that will complete my comment on this question. Thank you. Mr. Djidic, Marko Prskalo, when did he tell you this, on what day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was 16th or 17th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was he acting in the capacity of a negotiator with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was Pilicic with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran Pilicic was him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: They were assistant parliamentarians of General Blaskic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to them when they returned from their mission as parliamentarians and were entering the Vitez hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard about it, about the wounding. I do not know exactly who was wounded, was it Marko or Zoran.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you heard that a sniper from Stari Vitez had hit the two parliamentarians when they were entering the Vitez hotel where the headquarters of the command was situated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that at the next day's joint meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you give the orders to shoot at the parliamentarians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you know that they would be shot at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you learnt about it, did you start proceedings to investigate the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did investigate, and I was given assurances that it was not a sniper that had shot at them; and I told the HVO side and the UNPROFOR that it was quite feasible that the gentlemen who was hit was hit by a stray bullet, which may have even been fired from the position of the church. There are no -- there is no reliable evidence that it was a sniper, and I am sure that a sniper was not operating. And if the shot had come from army positions I can assert that the soldiers told me that they had not fired. The person may have been hit by an ordinary rifle shot, because, from the army positions to that spot where the gentlemen was hit, the distance is no more than 150 to 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Therefore, the entrance to the Vitez hotel was under your fire control?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were able to control it for a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But what is your comment to the fact that both parliamentarians were hit only 50 metres before the hotel entrance after they had come out of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I condemn that. I still do. I carried out an investigation and it did not produce any results.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, that would be all for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will take our break now and resume at 11.45 am. (11.20 am) (Short break)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please bring in the accused, and the Defence, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, but on the transcript it said "45", so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Registrar, is there a problem with the accused?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, we have one mystery cleared up. The transcript did say "11.45". We can now resume Mr. Nobilo. As far as the schedule goes, where are you now, can you tell us where you go?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: All day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All day. All right, yes I understand. Since we are not taking any authority away from the Prosecutor, for that reason we give you all the time you need and we can deal with this on a more general issue at other times. All right, proceed Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djidic, shall we go back to your investigation in connection with the attempted assassination of two parliamentarians Pilicic and Prskalo. In that investigation, did you take into consideration the fact that Pilicic and Prskalo were running for 50 metres to the entrance to the hotel, surrounded by UNPROFOR officers. This was an element that you took into consideration in your investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not familiar with the details, when and how these officers were surrounded, but I can assert that at that time an attack was going on in Stari Vitez, and these attacks went on continuously. Only exceptionally was there a lull.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you take into consideration that Pilacic and Prskalo who were running for 50 metres from the entrance of the hotel surrounded by UNPROFOR officers, that both of them were hit with two bullets each, and not one of the UNPROFOR officers was hit? Did you take that into consideration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And if you had known that, what would have been your conclusion? Was this a sniper or four stray bullets, not one, four?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what my criminal police would have done. I think I was told that one of these officers was hit in the thigh, and another one from the same bullet in the arm, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you mean, one bullet hit two men, one in the thigh and the other in the arm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the information that I received.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And your officers did not inform you that Pilacic was hit in the arm and the leg and Prskalo in the thigh and in the leg?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go back for a moment to the kidnapping of the people in Zenica, do you remember any press conference on Vitez television on 15th April 1993, when Blaskic and Kordic participated in connection with that kidnapping?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not watch that programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 15th April 1993, the day before the beginning of the conflict, was Dzemal Merdan from Zenica at your headquarters, he was deputy commander of the Third Corp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. From the church to the hotel you said that the bullet may have strayed from the church. What is the distance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is 500 to 600 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In your testimony you mentioned that General Blaskic was wearing a black uniform when the unit was being lined up by Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Among Croats and Catholics, does black clothing have any other meaning apart from the interpretation that you gave in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My neighbours, Croats, before the war, would wear black suits when there was a death in the family.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And when you would go to a funeral, what kind of clothing would one wear on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The immediate family would usually wear black suits.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And not others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Talking about the oath, do you recall the text of the oath that had to be taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember the exact wording, but this oath was made for Herceg-Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you describe what it was like? Would somebody read it and others repeat? And who did one make that solemn statement to? What was the ceremony like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was Mario Cerkez who would read the text, and the fighters, the soldiers would repeat after him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would he report to anyone? Would he address anyone? Would he salute anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that Mario would report to Kordic. I am not quite sure of that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was Kordic in civilian clothes, or in uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You spoke to us about the speech made by Kordic and others, and you said that at the time you could not believe that anyone could say anything like that, and if anyone else had told you about it you would not have believed him. Have I remembered well what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you tell us when this swearing in took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the summer of 1992. I do not recall the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And your disbelief, to remind you, was regarding the division of peoples within a multi ethnic Bosnia. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said you did not believe. But what had happened in Bosnia by then, what happened with the Serbs and the attack on Sarajevo? Had not the separation already started, and the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina? Was there not bloodshed already before then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who was fighting whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosnia-Herzegovina was attacked by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the domestic, the Bosnian Serbs participate in this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they did, as well as Serbs from Vitez because in the course of 1992 they would go somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How, then, do you explain your statement that if somebody had told you you would not have believed that the people would separate like this when interethnic conflicts had already broken out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Vitez and throughout central Bosnia there were not many Serbs. The Croats and Muslims had lived together for centuries. I have already spoken about that life that we had together; and I did not believe that the words such as those uttered by Kordic, that this was historically Croatian land, and that it will be Croatian land. I could not believe that there were such people, and I said I would not have believed anyone if they had told me about it, if I personally had not heard and seen it on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I did not quite understand what troubled you when Kordic said it was a historically Croatian land. Did he say it was exclusively the land of Croats, or is the problem that you do not accept that Bosnia is also historically Croatian land?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was troubled because he was talking about historical Croatian lands, when it is well known that Muslims were living there, too; and I think even before the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you tell me if you can remember, with precision, did he say that this was the land of Croats only, or did he say it was Croatian land?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On a number of occasions in answer to a question from the Prosecution, you said that the headquarters of General Blaskic's command was at the Vitez hotel. My question is: do you know when General Blaskic set up his headquarters, his command, at the Vitez hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know the exact date. I know that for a time he was in Kruscica, in the Lovac Hotel. And later he moved to the hotel in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you do not even know approximately what time of year it was when he moved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was in the summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would you be surprised to learn that it was in Christmas 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For Christmas?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: His headquarters not the local HVO command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not be surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that Kruscica was a predominantly Muslim or Croat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Predominantly Muslim locality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that you spoke to Colonel Blaskic by phone in connection with the six policemen detained in Kruscica. Did you call Mr. Blaskic or did he call you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At 6 o'clock in the morning I called up Mr. Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you have another conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was another conversation, when I was called up by Pasko.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But with Colonel Blaskic did you have a conversation before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I spoke to him about 3 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The threat that was made, was that during the conversation at 6 o'clock, or at 3 am?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was threatened both at 3 and at 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: By Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, by Pasko at 3 and by Colonel Blaskic in the morning at 6, and I think there was another threat during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By Pasko.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me try to put to you a question to organise a little bit your testimony. When did you become a member of the command of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was at the end of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What position did you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who was your superior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander was Hakija Cenjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell me who were the members of the command, what positions they had, and their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hakija was the commander. I was the chief of staff. The person in charge of security I think was Sigred Avdic. Mobilisation and general affairs, Senadar Karsavic. Commander of the military police, I think, was Anto Korumdjija. Assistant for logistics was Muhamed Patkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That was the complete TO staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure I have mentioned everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In the course of 1992, were there any changes, personnel changes, within this group of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What were the changes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think Mario Palanez left and did not work for the staff any more. He is the one with the notebook, Eniz Varupa, Eniz Varupa, and I do not recall any more changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But we met him in the military police of the HVO, I think?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Korumdjija left the TO staff, I am not sure, but I think this was in August or September of 1992. I am not certain about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, please, what was the responsibility of the TO staff in this period of 1992, if we can be more specific. What were its main tasks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The main tasks of the TO star was to send people to the front, to form regional detachments, or rather to form an army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about the arming, did that go through the staff? What was the method of arming the TO in 1992 or of the Bosniaks in Vitez, because we said there was the Patriotic League as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We armed ourselves in every conceivable manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you please describe the most typical ways of the procurement of weapons in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know all the details, since I joined the army, or rather the TO in May. But I do know that most of the armaments was taken from the warehouse in Slemeni, both Croats and Muslims took those weapons. This was a joint operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How much weaponry was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that warehouse, the weaponry was housed, of the Territorial Defence, from the whole of central Bosnia. A part of the weapons was destroyed because members of the former JNA had blown up those warehouses. And there were many damaged weapons that were later repaired. Later on --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell us roughly how many pieces there were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not like to engage in any guess work.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it more or less than 5000?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there was more than 5000.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So other forms of arming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the methods was purchase of weapons from Croats, a private organisation that was set up in Vitez, it is called Vitez trade, at the time sold weapons. That is something that I heard about. I personally did not purchase any weapons from this company.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What did you hear about them? Where did they get those weapons from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was coming from Croatia, or via Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me: was there any individual procurement in addition to the methods you have mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where did individuals get their weapons from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By purchasing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both in Vitez and in the surrounding localities, and especially from people who were coming from those places which had been captured by the Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Those people coming from places captured by Chetniks, how did they have weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The people of the Jajce, in particular, when Jajce fell, they brought with them a great deal of weapons, and one could buy them for -- at a very low price.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The TO had its logistics, of course. Did the TO later on procure any weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From those refugees, some from the Croats, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you send your representatives to do the purchasing in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did any weapons reach you from the government in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, in 1992 you have a TO staff. Who is among your superiors from the competent political structures? To whom are you answerable in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Superior to me was the municipal, or the regional staff in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In terms of structure yes, they were superior to you but were you really accountable to any executive or political body in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First the municipal staff was accountable to the mayor, and later, when the functions were separated and Croats and Muslims worked independently of each other, then my superior was the President of the War Presidency in Vitez, on the political side. And, again, the regional staff in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The War Presidency existed in 1993, but in the end of 1992 were you answerable to the coordination council for the protection of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, both to the council and to the War Presidency, which also existed in 1992, or maybe I am confused here, but the council did exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were you answerable to them as a political body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You referred to the staff of the Territorial Defence of Vitez. Who was your superior, the regional staff of Zenica, you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who was superior to the regional staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was the republican staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who was the TO republic staff answerable to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Directly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the Minister of Defence in the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina have any authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that the Republic staff was answerable to the presidency. I am asking you: did any power belong to the Minister of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So did you answer directly to the presidency, or to the Minister of Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who the republic staff of the TO was directly answerable to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You named members of the staff, and their functions, which were lower forms of organisation than the municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were regional detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you enumerate them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The municipal staff then had 11 regional detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you enumerate them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can try. That was the regional detachment of Vitez, regional detachment of Bila, regional detachment of Ahimici, of Kruscica, of Poculica, of Preocica, regional detachment of Novaci, and I think there was a regional detachment of Donja Veceriska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: These regional detachments, how many conscripts did they have? How many soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know the exact figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can I please ask the usher to take these documents from me? (Handed). Please put this on the ELMO, then we will read it out together. So, can we improve the contrast a little bit? Sir, in the upper left corner there is a stamp which says "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina municipal staff of the Territorial Defence number 05-2201/92" the date is 15th August 1992 "Vitez". Numerical signs of the commanding units of the municipal staff of defence of Vitez, communicates to the security. The word "security", is given in handwriting in the right corner. We communicate to you the numerical signs of the command and units of the municipal staff of defence of Vitez. Then it says defence staff of Vitez, number 8179/1. Security or protection staff squadron 8178/12. Then detachment of TO. It says detachment of Visoko Hakija Djellvic. Then follows TO detachment in brackets battalion Vitez. Then 8444-3 Dubravica; H44-4, Poculica; 8444-5 Busovaca; 844-6 Han Kompanija; 844-7 Bila; 844-8 Stari Vitez; 844-9 Kolonija; 8444-10 Kruscica; 8444-11 Vraniska. Anti-sabotage platoon 8647. Liaison unit 9510/11. Logistic space 9215. Battery of LAB and anti-aircraft defence 8957. Signed chief of staff for OMPP Causevic Zenada." Mr. Djidic, do you recall this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do remember this document. I do not remember the figures, but I roughly remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who was the Zenada Causevic who signed this. It says above the signature OMPP, what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It means assistant for organisational and administrative affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was she discharging this function?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you recognise this stamp as yours, maybe you can see it on the ELMO, the stamp in the upper left corner, was that how your system of numbers and signs looked? You can see it on the original?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot see it clearly, but I think that is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell me, the protection and staff platoon at that time, how many soldiers did it have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me in terms of structure, a battalion, how many soldiers did it have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were units of 200 to 400 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does it mean in terms of TV structure, a detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The number of soldiers varied in such units. A detachment as such could not be qualified in terms of numbers, and not unlike the way it was in the previous army, where there was particular number of soldiers in a battalion, a platoon a detachment. The number varied from place to place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But a detachment was envisaged as part of the TO structure, and what was the range of variation in your territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were detachments with 30 soldiers, and even less depending on the density of population, and some detachments, on the other hand, had up to 100 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, the liaison unit, who it was headed by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of material and resources were at the disposal of the communications unit -- the signals unit, sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they had the old RUP3.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a radio transmitter receiver, Radio 12 and Radio 30. We also had hand-operated radio stations, mainly used by the military police and the units on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like, Mr. Usher, to put up a map on this board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: First, Mr. Nobilo, first we have to settle what is to become with this previous document. I suppose it will be handled the same way, since you did not indicate the source. Therefore, we will ask the Registrar to mark it as D20.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I agree with you, Mr. President, but I should like to draw to your attention the fact that the witness has confirmed both the stamp and the authenticity of this document, and the source is the staff of the Territorial Defence of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We have already had this discussion and the Trial Chamber decided that -- it is not because in his statement the witness has authenticated a document which means that that is enough. If you officially state where you get it from it is not the stamp which identifies it, but at the end of the day it is the source of the document itself. That has to be identified. This was not indicated, I suppose that the document will remain with the same status as the previous ones, going from 15 to 20. Do you agree with that, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In that case, we reserve our right to identify it at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. We can now move to the following document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I should now like to ask the witness ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps we could give you some kind of device that would allow you to be close to the map and ask your question without having to go through complicated gymnastics.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo is a famous athlete, your Honour, I think he can do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Okay, if we could help though. Mr. Kehoe, do you wish to make an objection? This is the feeling I think I have here. Mr. Kehoe, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, are we going to get a copy of this map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, I would suppose so. Mr. Nobilo, do not you have a copy of the map for the Prosecution? Do you not have a copy of this map for the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Mr. President. I have only one copy, and we can later make copies for everyone. We are offering this as evidence. This is a military map, but for next time we shall try to provide copies. This is a map --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry, I cannot hear Mr. Nobilo because he is far from the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We have just identified this map. It comes from headquarters, is that what you said? Be more specific. You obtained this map from headquarters or? It should be indicated somewhere. You did not make the map so I think you can simply read. Tell us, Mr. Nobilo, where this map comes from. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, this is a map of -- made by the Yugoslavia People's Army on a scale of 1: 50,000, which was widely used in all of the former Yugoslavia and it could be found in more or less all the staffs of the Territorial Defence and units of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, as regards the identification I do not think there would be any objection to it being an exhibit. There is a problem because you do not have it and I think you have to have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is the problem, Mr. President. With all due respect to counsel I would like a copy so I could follow along with this cross examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This will now be admitted as an exhibit, but you have to continue the cross-examination. I do not completely agree with you, Mr. Kehoe. It will be on the ELMO. As regards with your question you have said in order to continue this cross-examination you need it to follow. You can follow the way we are. However, I think if you are suggesting that you have a right to reply later on after the cross-examination, it means that any possible right to reply means that you are going to also have the map. If there is only one copy then the Defence must lend it to the Prosecution. Mr. Nobilo, I think we have completed with that incident. Let us not waste any more time. We are wasting a lot of time, please. It is settled. It is an exhibit. It has been accepted as such. You can have it for your reply. Now you may continue the -- you can follow the cross-examination on the monitor the way all of us are doing. That is the end of this incident. Mr. Nobilo go on. Mr. Kehoe, we have to go forward. It is 25 after 12. We have another half a day. There are questions for the judges, there is a reply. That is enough. The map is here. Everybody can see it. Mr. Nobilo, please continue with your cross-examination. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I suggest, perhaps that the Prosecutor approach, too, and be present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That is a good suggestion which could have been made immediately, we would have saved 10 minutes. Gentlemen, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, do you know this -- are you familiar with this type of --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Our colleagues need to hear the translation. If we can have a moment to get everyone outfitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this type of map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In your work, did you use this type of map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You told us the names of the detachments from 1992. Can you tell us the command positions of those detachments by indicating them with a sign of some sort, the village where they were, so that we can have an idea of how they were distributed, the detachments they came under the command of your TO staff. You are familiar with this system so will you please explain what exactly you are indicating. So first of all the headquarters of the Territorial Defence staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we call it STO? Where is the Vitez battalion, the command post of the Vitez battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Vitez battalion, at that time, and the volunteer Vitez detachment were at Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But where was their command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you please indicate Kruscica? So that was the detachment of Vitez "O" standing for Odred and "V" for Vitez. You said there was a battalion, too, which came under this command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well, can you indicate the other detachments that you listed? For the benefit of the transcript Bila detachment, so that is Bila, that is another detachment there. What was the next, the one Dubravica, where is that? So we will mark it with a circle. A circle indicating "O" for Odred and underlining the place of the -- underlining the name of the place. The next detachment Tolovici, a circle, underlining the name of the place, detachment Ahimici, we are underlining the name Ahimici and marking it with a circle. Next. Can I help you, tell me the name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Detachment Donja Veceriska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So we are underlining the place and marking it with a circle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Next the Dubravica detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We will underline the word Dubravica and mark the position with a circle. Let us look at the list. Han Kompanija that is the Dubravica detachment. We have marked that. What about Poculica? We underline the word Poculica and we mark it with a circle. Bila, we have identified. Kolonija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is here (Indicates). It was in town. So Kolonija detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about Vraniska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We underline the word Vraniska and we mark it with a circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You have listed some other, other detachments, I think, can you remember them? Is it possible, please, Mr. Registrar, to go back to the statement of Mr. Djidic when he enumerated the detachments. Can we look that up in the transcript, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The names are mispronounced, I am afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In any event, these detachments that you mentioned in 1992, did they remain unchanged? Can you tell us for how long this system was in effect, until what date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This system lasted, I think, until the autumn of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What month roughly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the brigade was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you tell us roughly the month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was November.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Therefore, can we write on this map, November 1992, until November 1992, can we put that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to tender this map as evidence if there is no objection from my learned colleague?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Your colleagues have expressed reservations which were indicated, for the time being the Tribunal has now decided that this map will be an exhibit and asks before any reply is given that copies be distributed, if the Prosecution needs it of course. Turning to the Prosecution we are admitting this map as D21, which the Registrar will hold. Can everybody sit down now. You do not need everyone to be standing up now, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, in this situation we have only a single map marked in that way. Can we have it copied in collaboration with the Registry, because we cannot have the other copied marked like this, only copied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. For the time being we will make copies of that map, and I think that should be enough. Proceed, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, the district staff of Territorial Defence of Zenica, who was the commander in 1992, in the period up to November 1992 that we have been talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander was Mr. Dzemal Merdan.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who was the deputy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the deputy was Vinko Barisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who were the members of the regional staff of TO Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell us, from which municipalities the regional staff of Zenica united, which municipal staffs the regional staff covered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zepce, Vitez, Busovaca, Novi Travnik, Travnik, Bugojno, Gornji Vakuf. I do not know if I have left anything out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: 6 Kaknjo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
