utterances.text: You can see the lines here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well, and then is it this side or the other side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can I draw a straight line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well, and then -- was the stadium inside, can you show us how you went from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I apologise. It went along here, not over there, a correction. So we will correct that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can I go to the end of the stadium?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This far.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What are we going to do with the stadium, are we going around it, like this, across the stadium or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I draw a line across the stadium, how am I going to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Like this, and then along here, along the edge of the houses. Here (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where is your line? Where is your line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here. That would roughly be the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And this here, can I link these two lines, no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think this far roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. This line, somewhere around here, like this, it encompasses the houses. These two lines should be deleted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know the names of the streets where the line was going through the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you tell us from this point here, that is in the direction of the hotel, to the most distant point, what was the distance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: About 500 metres. That is the main road from the beginning of the territory under your control to the end, the distance was 500 metres. What were the lateral points where the distance was the greatest between two lateral points?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 600 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So it is about 500 by 600 metres. How many inhabitants were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, about 1,600 inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Fine. Could we now -- I am not a military man, but were there any particular points of resistance where you concentrated your fire power?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you established your defence lines, where were the main points of resistance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The line was more or less evenly manned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you did not have troops that were concentrated in particular places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were covered in the main directions of defence, roughly this part (Indicates). Can we put an arrow here, yes? So the HVO would be coming from here and from the church, from Lavici like this, and from the school. That was where most of the attacks came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And were the heaviest attacks where you concentrated the largest number of forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where was your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was here (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was the name of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a private house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So this is the headquarters. What about the military police? Where was it housed? Where were its headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The military police was accommodated in the same building as the civilian police, the Fire Brigade centre. I think it was here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So the civilian and military police, we will mark them with the letter P for the centre of the civil and military police. Where was your warehouse, your logistics base?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was here (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Outside the line or within the line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So for the logistics base we will put the letter L. What about the communications centre, it was within the headquarters. Where did the troops have their meals, was there a particular place, or were they fed in the households?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had very little troops, but we had a common canteen near the headquarters. So here we have the canteen (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We will put the letter K for the word cooking hut in Croatian or canteen. Will you tell me where the army slept, were there any barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The military and the civilian police were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about the other military troops, where did they sleep?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They slept in their houses, they were local people so they all went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. Did you have a staff detachment, a protective staff detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, about 10 soldiers, and they kept guard duty around the headquarters, but they went home when they were off duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us: where did the -- where were the troops stationed when they were in reserve, when they were not on duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In the spring of 1993, from the 18th, 19th onwards during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So there was no particular place. Did you have all the army deployed in the trenches during the fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So those who were not on the Defence lines, were they together somewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they slept, at their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you have any bunkers? Did you build any bunkers during those 11 months?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you show us where they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Round the whole of Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: These are trenches. But bunkers, I am talking about bunkers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All around Stari Vitez. No, there were not bunkers everywhere and the distance between them depended on the terrain. There was about 50 metre distance between two bunkers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is going too fast, your Honour, and we are missing the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Of course, these are very important questions for you, Mr. Nobilo, I assume?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, very important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I think we can go back to our seats now. Tell me please, Mr. Djidic, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The foil, Mr. Nobilo, do you wish to tender it as evidence, as you have indicated the defence lines under instruction from the witness? Let me repeat: do you wish to have the foil integrated in the records as evidence what do you want to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, but I would like it to stay there for a little longer, if need be. Mr. Djidic, when speaking about the number of troops, you said that you had 50 to 100. You were the commander for 11 months. Can you give us a precise answer? How many troops did you have? You said that some were your own, some were attached to the staff, some were at home, that some troops from the brigade were on vacation, on leave. Can you tell me if we include the military and civilian police how many troops did you have at your disposal during these 11 months of seige?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between 200 and 250 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When the seige began, did you mobilise additionally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And those additionally mobilised are included in the 250?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The armaments. In addition to infantry weapons, did you have any other weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What did you have that was not infantry? I am not talking about rifles. What else did you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had a 60 millimetre mortar, with only 10 shells; and RPG, with about 10 shells, and nothing else in terms of heavy weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In the night, when the attack occurred, or rather at dawn, did you have patrols out in the streets of Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They should have been there. Some were, but by the morning it emerged, later, that almost all of them were asleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the aerial photograph, we can see trenches. When did you regulate the defence line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We worked on it, even three months later.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When did the more important works begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They began after we had buried the dead people from Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was on the 26th or 27th of April, 1993. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: From the 16th April, until the 26th or 27th, when you started on these major works, how did you defend yourselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People hid behind houses, behind sheds, behind trees, in certain ravines around the stadium fences.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You are talking about private homes and sheds?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In relation to Vitez hotel, you said that the line of defence was about 150 metres. Did your units get any closer during the battles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So the closest you got to Hotel Vitez was 150 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that the distance was 150 to 200 metres; but my troops did get closer to the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How close did they get?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They reached the administrative building of the utilities administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How far is that from the hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is about 80 to 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall exactly, but these were actions taken on their own initiative. Mostly the troops were looking for cigarettes and alcoholic drinks. They did not stay long in that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that on 16th April your headquarters were hit. Did you change the location after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where did you move?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I moved 100 metres within Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: To what location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same location, but 100 metres removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It was a private house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a private house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you please show us on the map where your headquarters were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicates) I think it was here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I have marked this with the letter Z1. So I have marked it with Z1, the new headquarters. You said that you moved your headquarters by 100 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But if the whole width is 600 to 700 metres then it seems to me to be too close?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you can measure it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. You mentioned the houses that were hit with the fire extinguishers, the babes. Could you tell us which were the houses that were hit, and in which street, I want to be specific?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry. I did not hear the answer, could the witness please repeat the answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I believe the translator did not hear the answer, and did not translate, because the question is running over the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Please, Mr. Nobilo, could you repeat your question, and allow the interpreters to do their job?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I asked whether you could indicate the houses that were hit with the explosive devices made from fire extinguishers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that very few houses were not hit with the explosive devices, or almost hit, in other words they fell very close to the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Therefore, could you please, as an example, indicate some of the houses and give us the names of the owners, or the address? The houses that were hit with these fire extinguishers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: These houses which were hit by converted fire extinguishers --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me counsel. (Pause).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The houses which were hit by converted fire extinguishers shall be marked with points?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you so wish then you should -- then there would be many points inside Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But to save time let us begin with 10 houses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, I have to intervene. The witness will answer as he wish, but it is rather complicated, if not difficult, to distinguish houses which are hit, the identity of the owners and so on. The map we have is an aerial one. Perhaps you could simplify the question and ask an indication of a few houses as an example. Surely it is difficult to provide a whole list, as the witness has answered. So, please, let us speed up this part of the question, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You can see better from closer quarters, and the witness would perhaps be able to do that. We can do it in another way. I will be showing you particular quarters and the witness will tell me whether the converted fire extinguishers hit them or not. I am showing you this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That is better now. That is better.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am marking it with number 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I help? Your Honour, allow me to lend what assistance I can?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, you may, yes, you may, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What you see now will be the places hit by explosive device (Indicates). Everything. Absolutely everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You did not point exactly, you did it randomly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, because the entire territory was hit by a multitude of explosive devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, the catapult launching these so-called fire extinguisher and the fire extinguisher converted into an explosive device, in which way does it fly? Does it fly in a direct, in a straight line or in an arch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In an arch.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does this device launched in such a manner -- is it able to fly over a two storey building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, tell me, what is the range of this device?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it is 3 to 400 metres, and it can also fire at a closer change, and at a longer range, I think. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Asked by the Prosecutor you said you had enough ammunition. Did you have a military warehouse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did, a small warehouse, which was a backup we issued to people who went to the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Throughout 11 months a lot of it was used up, how did you refill it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We got new ammunition from captives and we took the ammunition people held in houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the UNPROFOR bring any ammunition and military equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who is General Alagic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: General Alagic is commander of the VII Corp, he was commander of the VII Corp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was he also commander of the III Corp at one point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was he commander of the operative group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Operative group Krajina. I have a document your Honour. I kindly ask the usher to approach. (Handed). The President, your Honours, an the first page the article is about Ljiljan. This is a newspaper close to the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and this issue is from last week, the date is the 23rd July, 1997 -- sorry, 30th July 1997. The pages we copied have on them war memories of General Alagic who wrote a book "War in central Bosnia". On page 27, the third page in my copy, page 27 in the newspaper, please put it on the ELMO on the right-hand side, next to the photograph of the commander of the 17th Krajina brigade we can read: "The army was blackmailed by the seige of Stari Vitez where fear reined from the massacre against Bosniaks." The text goes on. "On the other hand you were blackmailed" quote unquote, by Stari Vitez and General Alagic's exactly. Our pressure on their lines had always the purpose of deterring them from entering Stari Vitez, because we were afraid that a more horrible massacre could occur there than the one in Ahmici." Then follows the text which is important and is the reason why I brought this exhibit: "Thanks to our connections in the United Nations, we managed to bring some resources into Stari Vitez to enable them to defend themselves, and at the same time, by long range artillery, we have foiled defences of the HVO against Stari Vitez. The evidence of Stari, even women were engaged in the Defence". I would like you to admit this newspaper into evidence, because that source is well known. I can provide the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is counsel arguing that General Alagic is talking about these resources that UNPROFOR brought ammunition in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I am afraid I cannot get involved in the question of the translation, but the question now is whether we can admit it as evidence. I think we can. We know what the source is, and you can contest it as you wish. Mr. Registrar, what is the number of this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, Mr. Alagic claims that arms were smuggled to you through the UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So General Alagic is not saying the truth. Did UNPROFOR come to Stari Vitez during the seige?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: With what intention? What was their objective?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To organise meetings, escorting humanitarian aid and escorting the International Red Cross to enable evacuation of the wounded and to reach agreements on various exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is it true, as General Alagic says, that even women were mobilised in the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were women in the first aid units, and in other areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, are you familiar with the public appeal of the HVO to all women, children, elderly people -- not the appeal, excuse me, their statement that they are free to leave Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was that accepted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not by me and not by anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because people did not want to abandon their houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you not think that that was the way to avoid civilian casualties because we are talking about civilians here, not the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe that was possible before the funeral, not after it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you propose at least the civilians to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you not think it was your duty to propose that to people for the sake of saving them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To propose to them to leave their houses?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, but for a purpose, to save their lives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody -- it was impossible to leave Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: There was a proposal of the HVO from April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People did not want that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were there any more such proposals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you agree with my statement that at any stage of the fighting HVO allowed civilians to leave Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, when did that cease to be possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were certain periods when it was not possible, nor were there any agreements or proposals to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And were these periods relieved by other periods when it was possible to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: HVO allowed for a certain time civilians to leave, and at one point most civilians had abandoned Stari Vitez, but not those who had houses in Stari Vitez. They did not want to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And could you order them to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think I was able to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Have you ever tried?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me about the wounded. How did you evacuate them when you evacuated them at all, through whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of the wounded civilians were not evacuated. Some of them were evacuated with the assistance of the International Red Cross, who came escorted by the UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You referred to two cases when people died because evacuation had not been permitted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think there were only two such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How many were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly, but there were many.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell me the names of the people and the time when it happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not list all of them. But I could remember quite a few of them. One of such casualties, one of the people who died, the most typical example, perhaps, is a child only two years old. There were more civilian victims, women and elderly people, but also military men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us come back to the child. What was the date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I have it written somewhere. If your Honour would allow me to look at my papers. (Pause). That was on 28th November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who did you approach to request permission for evacuation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We requested that through the 325th Brigade, who was in touch with the UNPROFOR. UNPROFOR arrived only two days later. The child had already died.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you have a direct contact with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No telephone contacts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, our telephone did not work from the 10th day of the conflict to the end of the war. All telephones were dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you have any other line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not with the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly, you called up the 325th Brigade, they called the UNPROFOR and the UNPROFOR arrived two days later; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know what the situation was in Vitez, because you mentioned famine in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you hear about the convoy at Bijeli Put?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When did that convey reach Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember the exact date, one truck, which belonged to that convey reached Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who organised that convey?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was organised by Caritas, an Islamic religious organisation in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who was the leader of the convey?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The convey which reached Vitez was Bijeli and Sefkjia, I do not know his last name, but he is the principal man in the mosque in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could his name by Omerbasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: They reached Stari Vitez, and who was the leader of the entire white convoy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, I think it was Larry Hollingworth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does the name of Dr Lang mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was he there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not come to Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was he one of the leaders of that convoy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said you were under artillery fire of the HVO. Could you mark artillery positions of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can is the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, again, on this foil, again on this foil, which is now covering the aerial photograph of Stari Vitez, we shall mark the artillery positions of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stari Vitez was under fire most of the time from the direction of Krcevine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, but where are the artillery positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me counsel, you are speaking over him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Artillery positions shifted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you point out several typical positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can. That was in the area about the petrol station Kalen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I shall mark it with the letter T?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here (Indicates), near these houses, and then again here (Indicates), then here (Indicates). That would be approximately where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it one cannon moving, or were there several of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a number of artillery guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How many in this area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Depending on the period, I noted a 40 millimetre cannon, because my headquarters were hit from that side with the 128 millimetre launcher. There were also mortars of 40 and 60 millimetres, which fired on Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you have any more positions to show us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (Indicates) this area here (Indicates) is called Gradina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Which gun was placed here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was a hilltop cannon of some kind, and there were also other guns. After the capturing of the Gacice village, there was one position below the village from which they fired on us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it here? We shall mark it with a T and then a G for Gacice. What was placed here, which gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a 20 millimetre cannon, 40 millimetre cannon and mortars of a smaller calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember for now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were also fired at from the direction of the factory (Indicates). A long range cannon, 150 millimetres, I do not know where exactly it was positioned. We also had shelling of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: A cannon from the factory, what calibre was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was a 40 millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You had mortars. Where was it positioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We used it very rarely. The location was along the Lasva.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you indicate it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can. (Indicates) I am afraid it is not very precise, but I hope it can be accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: With the letter M we have marked the position of the mortar. Was that the only location it had, or were there others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is where we kept it, but it was not used. We used it very rarely, because we had very little -- few shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But it when it was used, did you move it to any other position from which you fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we used it at the Remiza, that is in the opposite direction. (Indicates). Later, in July 1993, when an armoured vehicle headed for Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were there any other locations from which you used the mortar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How is a mortar used? Is it placed on the front line, or is it further in the rear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends on the type you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Well, the type that you had, how is it properly used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That means in the trench with the infantry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How close?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 10 metres. Sometimes further than that. It was mainly a commando.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is a mortar positioned on an open area in the field, or is it protected in some way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is usually protected, sheltered.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What kind of shelter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does not have to be anything specially built.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But it must not be on a plateau on a flat area right next to the front line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I assume that the adversary could hit or rather the crew of the mortar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your assumption is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So it had to be sheltered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but it could be used from a place where there is no protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But is that the way it is usually used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Commandos, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mentioned the RPG, hand rocket launcher. How many shells did you have for this hand rocket launcher?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you tell me from which positions you fired these RPGs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were mostly these positions, along the line of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could we mark those positions, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could. (Indicates) here (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We will mark it with the letter R.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here and here (Indicates). We changed its position because we had only one of them, one RPG.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that you used the RPG along the main communication lines, and that you changed their position. What does that mean? Does that mean that you shifted from one side of the road to the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depended on the direction from which the attacks came. We were never sure whether another truck bomb could arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So we had these three positions, and did you change them round, those three points?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were those positions, mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In which semi-circle did you change the positions round those three points?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You told me that you changed positions, so I would like to know, we have these three points that you have indicated, within those three points did you change positions, or was the RPG always kept in one spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost always in one position.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you tell me in the course of 11 months, did you have any contact with the 325th Brigade, or rather did you receive information where that brigade was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you describe, over the months, where the 325th brigade was operating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is easy to describe. At the beginning of the war the lines changed little from what they were at the beginning of the war until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you explain where the 325th Brigade was, where the front was established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. That was not difficult to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to tender this foil as evidence, and we would complete the cross-examination regarding this foil, and then we can pass on to another map?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There are a couple of corrections I believe the witness made on this particular map, if you recall, counsel, so pending the corrections that are on the map. If we can hold this into abeyance until they are made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You are talking about the defence lines. Mr. Nobilo has a solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: With a blue marker we shall try to delete the surplus lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, please go up to the board, to the easel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is that correct now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The usher, could you help me, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The foil will bear which number, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Be careful of the marks, Mr. Usher, carefully. Mr. Nobilo and Mr. Prosecutor, it is now 5.25. Unless you are of a different opinion I think that even if we continue until 6 o'clock we will not finish with this witness. Mr. Nobilo, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am afraid we would not. You have seen that I am doing my best. I have left out a number of things, but these are all matters of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, but we have seen quite a number, but never mind, that is not the point. I think that you should put your last question, regarding this map. We will adjourn at 5.30 or as soon as you have finished with the questions regarding this map, and we will postpone the end of the cross-examination for the 18th August, at 10 o'clock. Mr. Nobilo, you may continue. If I said the 18th, it is the 19th of August, I am sorry. It is Tuesday, 19th August at 10 o'clock. I apologise for making a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, one further effort from you. The 325th Brigade. Where were their front lines in relation to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When was this? At what time?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Shall we start with April 1994 -- no, I apologise, 1993, April, 1993. With a blue marker I have indicated 4 as an indication of April 1993, and on top, 325, the number of the brigade. We are trying to obtain information regarding the confrontation line between the HVO and the 325th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the course of April, the situation changed. The line was not a permanent. I can try to give you an indication of only what I saw from Stari Vitez, and what I heard from colleagues from the 325th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am asking what would be the best way to mark these lines, from one place to the next, is that acceptable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between Ljubici and Tolovici. Here (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can I link the two lines, no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. It was here any way in Gacice, I do not know exactly. Then I think it went this way (Indicates). I do not know the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know this side, in this direction above Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know about Svbrino Selo, who controlled it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The army controlled it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can I mark a semi-circle there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is where my house is. (Indicates) here and then up here (Indicates) then this way (Indicates), and then this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Pirici, in whose hands were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you remember how these two parts were linked? Did it go along this road from Dubravica to Tolovici, Lazine who controlled Lazine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The HVO. The HVO controlled this far (Indicates). This is very approximate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you were in Vitez and the BH army was here. Do you know the situation here and here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see the lines up there, so anything I would say would not be reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about this road, going from Stari Bila to Tolvici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was controlled by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How far?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how far.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about Rijeka, who held that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the army held it. I think, I am not sure. I do not know how far the HVO controlled this territory, but later on the army controlled it. I do not know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we mark this region and this region as being under the control of the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can. Let me point out that this is not a precision map. You forgot to encircle Stari Vitez. Will you help me, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is that the situation as it was in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I was able to see, roughly. I do not know the line in the direction of Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That would be all regarding this map. And we would like to tender this map as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Boss, which number will this exhibit bear? Yes, thank you, we are going to adjourn the meeting now. Yes, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: With regard to this exhibit I believe it is more accurate to say post 16th April 1993. After the 16th April, 1993, not all of April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the course of April, but after the 16th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You wish to intervene Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Just before we break your Honour, because we are not going to have a hearing for two weeks I have a procedural question concerning the court's ruling at the hearing earlier this week. The ruling on the discovery motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The court had directed with respect to the August session any witness called by the Prosecution specified in my motion that notice of that be given in advance to the Defence as a temporary measure pending the final decision on the motion. I have spoken to the Prosecutor concerning how, in advance, that notice should be and there is no agreement on that issue. I would ask that the court direct that either the notice be 14 days in advance or at the time the Prosecution forms an intent to call one of those individuals, should it be less than 14 days before they are actually called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. First of all, we are going to ask the witness to withdraw. We are going to thank him and ask him to make another effort and come again on the 19th. Mr. Djidic, the Tribunal thanks you. We will ask the usher to accompany you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Registrar, can the curtains be drawn, and can we continue in camera? Yes, perhaps we do not need to draw the blinds, it is sufficient to have a private session, to switch off the sound. (Private session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Pages 1481 to 1488 in closed session
